key_insight: The paper argues that quantum circuits with classically verifiable substructure can be compiled more efficiently by agentic AI using fuzz-tested, certifiable optimization loops.
engineering_relevance: This matters because many high-cost quantum kernels in simulation, coding theory, and chemistry have structured subroutines that can be optimized more aggressively while preserving correctness guarantees.
method: Identify bottleneck subroutines with verifiable classical structure, such as reversible logic, phasing, and measurement-based uncomputation.
Use AI agents to search for improved circuit compilations and validate approximate synthesis through efficient simulation on classical inputs.
Apply the framework to three targets: 1/√x for Coulomb simulation, Reed-Solomon decoding, and quantum chemistry look-up tables/Givens rotations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reference implementations and a verification-oriented fuzz-testing paradigm, but does not provide quantitative benchmark results in the text provided.
watch_item: The approach depends on suitable input-distribution assumptions and on subroutines being sufficiently structured to support efficient classical verification.
paper_title: Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI
